# #2555 Early Review: Post-Call Result Authority Amendment

Binding review: issue2555/6016636495, early reviewed head55ff97676.
The user authorizes all three bounded repairs before any new server2 time.
This extends the original48-row class by three discriminating manifestations;
it does not replace their proofs, restart the gate, authorize another owner,
or establish class/PR closure. CI full / Local core plus named supplements
and the quiet BOTH-store numeric root remain binding. No PR is opened.

## Governing Contract

`platform-spec.yaml managed_agent_capability_surface.provider_turn.mock_workspace`
requires uncertain post-call projected results to stop the conversation without
model feedback or consuming its completion continuation. The adjacent
`forkchat_transport` requires the original frozen sandbox executor and forbids
live source substitution. The amended authoritative spec explicitly binds
projection to the context-selected executor and RPC-error classification to
the dispatched call. No runtime table, ledger, callback port, timeout retry,
compatibility behavior, driver fork or provider invocation is added.

## Exact Path And Owner Consumption

1. The existing conversation owns the response tool-call loop and its frozen
   fork dispatch, not the HTTP request. Registration preserves that authority.
2. The target-native mock worker sends one authenticated tools/call through
   `toolgateway.HTTPObservation`. `consumeRPCResponse` and its private
   `decodeRPCResponse` step are the sole decoder and response-attribution owner;
   `rpcResponseFailure` interprets only an exact-ID
   unambiguous error as a possible known pre-execution refusal. Discovery cannot
   execute an effect and may receive null-ID boot authentication refusal.
3. MCP `executorForContext` selects the existing ordinary or fork snapshot/stub
   executor. Dispatch already consumed it; `projectToolCallSuccessText` now
   consumes the same selected owner, never the global executor by convenience.
4. Successful tool execution precedes projection. Any later projection error
   is wrapped as ClassOutcomeUncertain, retaining its underlying cause. A known
   execution failure remains its own class. Complete role-scoped reads retain
   their fail-closed limits rather than gaining truncation or a new relay.
5. Ordinary oversized results use a relay only when the selected executor has
   the existing relay capability and read_file is currently callable. Otherwise
   the existing bounded preview has no follow_up path or invented file. The
   fork dispatch currently has no relay capability; none is added speculatively.
6. `MockRuntime.executeTransportTool` retains the wire envelope unchanged.
   `Conversation.resolveToolCalls` / `executeToolResponse` refuse uncertain
   transported outcomes before feedback, successor calls or model continuation.
   No second transport, result interpreter or model-round owner is introduced.

The old global projection call, ordinary post-success projection-error mapping,
foreign-error-before-ID interpretation and non-200 tools/call safe-refusal
inference are invalid. Existing parser/discovery bounds, token redaction,
exact standard RPC refusal controls and ordinary known-tool-failure handling
remain. RPC envelopes containing both result and error are ambiguous, not safe.
An unknown context-error number alone does not prove pre-execution refusal.

The PC50 library counterexample intentionally makes read_file callable on an
authority-valid frozen dispatch so it discriminates the formerly live relay
choice. The current canonical public fork policy has no read_file; the actual
public journeys qualify its bounded no-relay behavior, not a claim that the
global relay caused source corruption in that policy. No such corruption was
observed or inferred. Normal and oversized results remain separate controls.

## Proof Venues And Limits

The public fork journeys are internal retained H runtime composition with
real native workers, MCP HTTP, selected stores and public fork/chat APIs. They
are not compiled public serve/test or paid Claude/Telegram proof. A genuinely
large immutable entity field is declared as quoted initial text, not injected
with raw SQL or a synthesized projection. A real authored sibling has its own
intent, identity, completed setup occurrence and workspace sentinel.

Local host journeys passed on SQLite/PostgreSQL. The local bridge Docker attempt
correctly refused boot at target-local reachability; its red receipt stays red.
The subsequent real Docker positive uses the already-supported explicit host
network topology, not a production fallback or default-network credit. It proves
oversized result transport/continuation, not network-disconnect compensation.
The original non-oversized Docker root retains every original network-loss
assertion. The new Docker root is an individually named mandatory affected-path
supplement, excluded from ordinary no-Docker tier execution with no skip credit.
Hosted default-network Q01 and final qualification remain separately pending.

Initial test preparation errors (missing actor restoration hook, incomplete
known-failure detail, logical-vs-host backing-path comparison, duplicate sibling
intent and reading public operator request data as model input) are retained as
failed preparation receipts, not additional runtime defects. Corrected controls
use the existing actor hook/path owner and pinned model assertions. No original
assertion or deadline is relaxed. The original129 identity corpus and source-bound
ratchet remain required; no baseline or collector change is authorized here.

Watchlist decision: refine the existing transport_policy_and_surface_parity node
with post-success projection uncertainty, selected sandbox projection ownership
and response attribution. No new issue/node/POTENTIAL_ISSUES entry or broader
framework is warranted. Final focused receipts and immutable source head are
bound in the issue thread and swarm-docs evidence, not invented in this plan.

## Complexity And Confinement Preservation

The early-review correction does not waive the existing complexity ratchet.
Private same-owner steps separate RPC decoding, container creation and exact
stale-identity replacement. The transferred semantic-event observer keeps its
one original selected-store read transaction, exact SQL order, predicates,
failure admission and no-partial-evidence return while separating record facts
from pipeline-receipt decoding. The served debug observer's fixed SQL selection
is private; its query bytes, bounds, stage errors and presentation are unchanged.
No public query/transaction callback or generic fixture capability is introduced.
The descriptive authority registry records these exact private implementation
findings; neither the debt baseline nor its collector or classifier is changed.
Failed intermediate complexity/confinement receipts remain diagnostic evidence,
not qualification credit. Only the final committed-head green checks count.
